name: Memphis Hotfix
description: Drive a Memphis hotfix end-to-end with the cross-layer grid as a forcing function. Use when a bug may touch more than one layer — Rust core, NAPI bridge, TS host, CLI, doctor/status, tests — and paste the filled grid into the PR body. Skipping the grid is the number one source of dead-end fixes.
workflow: COLLECT: state the scope in one sentence, quote the operator where possible, and name the references (PR numbers, memory entries, postmortems) that anchor the fix.

GRID: walk every row of the cross-layer grid — Rust core, NAPI bridge, TS host, CLI, Tauri, doctor/status, tests — and mark each one ✅ (touches), – (does not) or 🔧 (transparent rebuild). A row without a verdict is an unfinished grid.
IMPLEMENT: make the change, narrow first, then broaden the test run.
VERIFY: run the tests for the touched surface, then the wider suite.
REPORT: paste the grid into the PR body and state what changed, what was verified and what risk remains.
promptHints: Ask the operator before coding when scope or affected layers are unclear.
A Rust change means the NAPI bridge row is 🔧 — the binary has to be rebuilt, and that is the memphis-rebuild-rust skill.
The tests row is ✅ always: at minimum a regression test for the bug being fixed.

examples.prompt: Napraw crash po zmianie w crates
examples.outcome: The skill fills the cross-layer grid first, so the Rust change, the NAPI rebuild, the TS rendering and the doctor hook are all decided before code is written.

notes: Memphis spans Rust core → NAPI bridge → TS host → CLI, TUI, HTTP, MCP and Telegram surfaces. A bug that looks Rust-only almost always has a TS-side rendering and a test grid.
Tier 0: no vault and no passphrase.
